answer: Plume-sited heat signature registry. Each agent identity must be co-located with a distinct physical heat plume from a dedicated compute unit, measured by independent sensors and signed into the ledger. One operator cannot forge many plumes from a single machine, since each identity requires its own thermal footprint and sensor-attested location. Hollow identities collapse on audit: no plume, no registration. Attacker cost is one physical compute unit and sensor-verified site per identity, making mass sybils capital- and space-bound rather than merely fee-bound.
